title: Harden Queue WebView trust and responsiveness
summary: Hardened the Queue WebView tab so large tables page predictably, row selection updates detail panels without rebuilding the table, local priority/order/override staging is visibly separate from backend launch scope, and filter/render warnings remain visible to operators.
reason: The Queue audit found ambiguity between local display state and backend launch scope, sluggish or disruptive large-table interactions, weak staging feedback for queue mutations, and file override actions that were too easy to mistake for immediate backend persistence.
behavior_before: Queue rows rendered as one large table, selection rerendered the full row set, manual order movement posted immediately, saved-policy override controls cleared backend fields immediately, and filter/render scope warnings could be easy to miss or overwritten by refresh status.
behavior_after: Queue rows render in capped pages with explicit page status, row selection updates visuals and detail panels locally, manual order and saved-policy override actions stage locally until Save, command buttons expose in-flight/dirty state, and scan/filter/scope guardrails remain visible.
manual_validation: python -m unittest selected Queue/static methods in tests.python.desktop.test_application_facade_web_static - passed
python -m unittest tests.python.desktop.test_application_facade_web_static -q - failed on unrelated Launch static assertions
rollback_plan: Revert the Queue WebView static asset, partial, smoke-test, and generated-summary changes listed in files_touched, then rerun the Queue browser smokes and change-control validation.
notes:
Implements the Queue UI audit fixes requested on 2026-06-18: visible filter/scope warnings, staged queue/order/override controls, async drawer guards, large-table behavior, semantic colors, and smoke coverage.
Full application facade static module still has unrelated Launch static assertion failures outside this Queue change.
